newsitem.title: USA: Dime to buy North American Mortgage.
newsitem.headline: Dime to buy North American Mortgage.

text.p: Dime Bancorp Inc. said Monday it agreed to buy North American Mortgage Co. in an all-stock transaction valued at about $374 million.
"This gets us where we want to be in terms of scale in the mortgage banking business," Dime President Lawrence Toal said in a telephone interview.

Toal had said at the Dime shareholders meeting in May that the company is transforming itself from a traditional thrift into a bank with emphasis in mortgage banking, consumer financial services, commercial real estate lending and other businesses. Now that the mortgage business has been expanded, he said, Dime can concentrate on broadening the other areas.

Fred Koons, chief executive of Dime's mortgage business, said that Dime is interested in expansion of mortgage products aimed at less creditworthy borrowers, an area which North American only recently started to roll out nationally.
Toal said North American's $8.3 billion in mortgage originations in the year ended March 31, and the combined $30 billion servicing portfolio, matches Dime's targets.
As part of the deal, Dime said it planned to buy back 6.9 million shares of its stock, or about 35 percent of the shares to be issued in the transaction.

Under the terms of the transaction, which will be tax-free to North American stockholders, 1.37 shares of Dime common stock will be exchanged for each share of North American common stock outstanding at the time of the closing.
Based on Dime's closing price on June 20, the ratio represents a value of $26.03 per share of North American common stock, for an aggregate transaction value of $374 million.
The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 1997. It must be approved by North American's stockholders and clear anti-trust review under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act.

Dime said North American had the right to terminate the agreement if the price of Dime common stock declined 20 percent or more. The agreement also grants Dime a "termination" fee of $15 million under certain circumstances.
Koons said Dime expects to achieve $18.8 million in cost savings in the acquisition.
Rich Mirro, who will be president and chief operating officer of the Dime mortgage business, said there will be some staff reduction at North American's California facilities.
Mirro did not provide any figures on the cuts.
North American originates mortgage loans in 31 states through a network of 107 offices.
The mortgage company will be headquartered in Tampa, Fla., and will operate under the North American name in most markets and the Dime name in selected markets.
